slides.title: Language focus: Passive voice (present & past)
slides.content:
The passive voice appears throughout this clip to describe what happens — or happened — to gold without always naming who does it. This shifts the focus onto the object or event rather than the agent, which is common in documentary and journalistic English.
• Form: use the correct tense of 'be' + past participle (e.g. 'is stolen', 'was melted down', 'were made').
• Meaning: the passive emphasises what was done rather than who did it — useful when the agent is unknown, unimportant, or deliberately vague.
• Use: in formal, academic, and documentary writing, the passive creates an objective, authoritative tone and is far more frequent than in everyday speech.
Next time you watch a documentary, listen out for the passive — it is one of the key tools that gives factual narration its confident, impersonal voice.
